live.name: Alchemy Uluwatu
live.verdict: Ubud's plant-based original, transplanted to a Bingin garden — raw bowls, an organic shop and yoga on the same grounds.

live.notFor: travellers set on meat or espresso-tonic party brunches

live.name: El Kabrón
live.verdict: Spanish cliff club above Pecatu's west coast — paella, an edge-of-the-world pool and Bali's most theatrical sunset seating.
live.whyHere: El Kabrón has run its 'Sunset Theater' on this cliff since 2011: a Spanish restaurant and pool set on a west-facing edge with nothing between you and the horizon. It is the occasion venue of the district — anniversaries, proposals, last-night blowouts.
live.whatToExpect: Minimum-spend seating tiers around a cliff-edge pool, a full Spanish kitchen (oysters, paella, tomahawk), and a sunset hour that books out. Despite the 'beach club' label there is no beach access — this is a cliff venue. Budget accordingly: it is one of the area's priciest tickets.
live.bestFor: special occasions; sunset dinner dates; celebratory groups
live.notFor: casual walk-in beers or families after a beach day
live.practicalNote: Jl. Pantai Cemongkak, Pecatu — between Bingin and Uluwatu.

live.name: Gooseberry
live.verdict: Modern French above Bingin Beach — foie gras and aged steaks by a pool, from long brunches to candle-lit dinners.
live.whyHere: Bingin's surf-shack shoreline hides one genuinely French kitchen up the hill: classic technique (snails, beef cheek confit, prime cuts) served poolside. It covers the widest arc of any dinner venue here — brunch through late dinner — without dropping its standards.
live.whatToExpect: Indoor-outdoor dining around a pool, a screen-free room by design, and a kitchen that takes French classics seriously. The same owners run the Gooseberry Intimates boutique next door — don't let the shopfront confuse the entrance. Evenings suit couples; the venue itself suggests earlier bookings for families.
live.bestFor: date nights; special occasions; a long French brunch after a Bingin surf
live.notFor: screens-out laptop sessions — the room is deliberately screen-free
live.practicalNote: Above Bingin Beach (Jl. Pantai Bingin area), Pecatu.
live.reservations: Book ahead for dinner; earlier slots work better with kids.

live.verdict: Minimalist Greek-inspired grill steps from Padang Padang — wood fire, natural wine and the Bukit's most confident new dinner room.

live.name: Single Fin
live.verdict: The Bukit's landmark cliff bar above the Uluwatu surf break — come for the swell and the sunset, not a quiet dinner.
live.whyHere: Every Uluwatu trip crosses Single Fin eventually: it hangs directly over the Suluban break, so you watch surfers thread the barrel while the sun drops. It has earned its place as the district's default sunset anchor.
live.whatToExpect: Terraced decks over the cliff edge, casual bar food, and a crowd that builds steadily from late afternoon. Wednesday and Sunday nights turn into full party mode with DJs and live acts running late; other evenings are more relaxed. Parking on the narrow Suluban lane is tight — come by scooter or drop-off.
live.bestFor: sunset drinks with the surf view; group nights out; post-surf beers
live.notFor: a quiet dinner for two, or working on a laptop
live.practicalNote: Arrive 60–90 minutes before sunset for a rail-side spot. Wednesday and Sunday are the big nights.
live.reservations: Mostly walk-in; tables go fast on Wednesdays and Sundays — reserve ahead for those.

live.name: Sundays Beach Club
live.verdict: A private white-sand cove at the foot of the Ungasan cliffs — the Bukit's one true toes-in-the-sand beach club.
live.whyHere: Most 'beach clubs' on this peninsula sit on cliffs. Sundays actually gets you onto the sand: a funicular carries you down to a sheltered lagoon with daybeds, watersports and evening bonfires. For families and beach days it is the district's clearest answer.
live.whatToExpect: Entry works as a daily beach pass with food-and-drink credit. Below the cliff you get calm, swimmable water (tide-dependent), kayaks and snorkelling gear, a beachfront kitchen, and bonfires after sunset. It is part of The Ungasan resort; the ride down is half the fun.
live.bestFor: beach days with kids; sunset bonfires; couples who want sand, not concrete
live.notFor: a quick cheap stop — the pass model rewards staying the day
live.practicalNote: Beach access is via the resort's inclinator from the clifftop. Check tides for swimming.
live.reservations: Daily beach passes are walk-in; cabanas and VIP set-ups are pre-booked.
live.where: Jl. Pantai Selatan Gau, Banjar Wijaya Kusuma, Ungasan

live.name: WAATU
live.verdict: Yakitori and open-flame cooking above Sundays Beach Club — everything over coals, nothing on gas.
live.whyHere: WAATU commits to one idea completely: every dish is cooked over fire — no gas, no electric burners. Chef James Viles runs archipelago ingredients through a yakitori lens on The Ungasan clifftop, making this the district's most distinctive serious dinner.
live.whatToExpect: A clifftop room at The Ungasan resort, skewers and larger cuts off the coals, and signatures like the wood-fired folded mortadella flatbread. Open from 11:00 until late; sunset slots pair naturally with a beach afternoon at Sundays below. Reserve through the venue's own page.

live.name: White Rock Beach Club
live.verdict: The big-format beachfront club on Melasti — pools, daybeds and a stage, directly on one of Bali's whitest beaches.
live.whyHere: Melasti's cliff amphitheatre is the south Bukit's most dramatic beach, and White Rock is the largest way to spend a whole day on it: infinity pools, rows of daybeds, dining decks and a proper events stage, day into night.
live.whatToExpect: A large venue that absorbs groups easily. Daybeds and suites work on a minimum-spend model credited to food and drink. The beach in front is white sand under high cliffs; the drive in comes down the carved Melasti cliff road, worth the trip on its own.
live.bestFor: group beach days; families with mixed ages; event nights
live.notFor: travellers after a small, quiet cove
live.practicalNote: On Melasti Beach on the south side of the peninsula — a real drive from the west cliffs, so plan it as its own half-day.
live.reservations: Reserve daybeds and suites via the club's booking site.

live.name: YUKI Uluwatu
live.verdict: Modern Japanese izakaya on the Labuan Sait clifftop road — sharing plates, wagyu sando and real dinner energy.
live.whyHere: YUKI brought its Canggu izakaya formula to the Bukit and it landed: a design-forward room, communal sharing plates and a bar programme that keeps tables loud in the right way. When the group can't agree, torched maki settles it.
live.whatToExpect: Sharing-format modern Japanese — sashimi, robata, the wagyu sando — open daily from 11:00 until late. The room leans social: bigger tables, music, occasion energy. WhatsApp reservations are the fastest route on busy nights.
live.bestFor: group dinners that need momentum; date nights; special occasions
live.notFor: a silent, slow tasting-menu evening
live.practicalNote: On Jl. Labuan Sait, Pecatu — minutes from the Uluwatu breaks.
live.reservations: Reserve via the official page or WhatsApp — weekends fill.

live.name: ZALI Uluwatu
live.verdict: Family-run Lebanese on the Suluban road — sharing feasts that work as well for kids as for a table of eight.
live.whyHere: The Bukit's dinner scene skews steak-and-sushi; ZALI widens it with an actual Lebanese kitchen — a native Lebanese chef, mezze spreads and grilled plates built for passing around. It is one of the few upscale-casual rooms here that genuinely fits families.
live.whatToExpect: A modern Levantine menu (hummus and mezze through samke harra), generous portions and a room that tolerates real conversation. Multi-branch family business — the Uluwatu branch sits on Jl. Pantai Labuan Sait near Suluban.
live.bestFor: group dinners over shared plates; early family dinners; date nights that need warmth over show
live.notFor: solo bar-seat dining
